steps.say: This defect is seen in 1 in 1500 to 3000 newborns and favours boys, so every maternity unit meets it. A third (33 percent) of babies arrive small, and 60 to 70 percent carry associated anomalies that shape survival. The feeding tube that will not pass remains the classic first clue.
steps.tx: **Oesophageal atresia** (blind ending gullet) with or without **tracheo-oesophageal fistula** (windpipe to gullet join) occurs in 1 in **1500** to **3000** births with mild male excess, a third (**33** percent) low birth weight, and **60** to **70** percent carrying **associated anomalies** (VACTERL defects) that dominate the prognosis.

vis.alt: Five Gross atresia types with coiled nasogastric tube X-ray, maternal polyhydramnios panel and VACTERL association features.
vis.caption: Atresia with fistula occurs in 1 in 1500 to 3000 births with associated anomalies in 60 to 70 percent. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The gullet and windpipe share one tube at 4 weeks, and faulty division leaves the classic pattern. One in 10 affected babies shows the VATERL cluster of vertebral, anorectal, tracheal, oesophageal, renal and radial defects. Proximal atresia with distal fistula, the C type, dominates every series.
steps.tx: Faulty **foregut division** (splitting of the shared tube) at **4** weeks causes the defects, **10** percent cluster as **VATERL** (vertebral, anorectal, tracheal, oesophageal, renal and radial anomalies), and the **C type atresia** (proximal blind pouch with distal fistula) dominates all Gross types.

steps.say: Drooling with choking on the very first feed should trigger the tube test at once. A catheter that recoils at the thoracic inlet is diagnostic of atresia, while maternal polyhydramnios in 86 percent flags pure atresia before birth. Air in the stomach proves a distal fistula is feeding the gut.
steps.tx: Drooling with choking on first feeds plus an **orogastric tube** (mouth to stomach catheter) recoiling at the thoracic inlet defines atresia, maternal **polyhydramnios** (excess amniotic fluid) is prominent in pure atresia at **86** percent, and distal fistula distends the stomach with air (**gastric distention**).

steps.say: Plain films answer the next question without any dye study, because contrast in the pouch can spill into the lungs. Abdominal gas confirms a distal fistula, while a gasless abdomen after failed tube passage means pure atresia. A contrast study with swallow is banned, and echocardiography with renal ultrasound screens the heart and kidneys.
steps.tx: **Abdominal gas** (stomach bubble on film) confirms a distal fistula while a gasless abdomen after failed tube passage means pure atresia, and a **contrast study** (swallow) is banned for aspiration risk. **Echocardiography** (heart ultrasound) plus renal ultrasound screen for cardiac and kidney defects.

vis.alt: Newborn neck and chest cutaway showing blind upper pouch with coiled feeding tube beside trachea and distal fistula.
vis.caption: Tube recoiling in a blind upper pouch with gastric air confirms the C type with distal fistula. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Nurse the baby upright and prone with the head raised, and keep the pouch empty with continuous suction. Sump suction with broad spectrum antibiotics is keeping the infant stable for theatre. Avoid routine intubation since positive pressure ventilation drives air through the fistula, and reserve gastrostomy with water seal for rescue.
steps.tx: Care is upright prone nursing with continuous **sump suction** (pouch drainage), broad spectrum antibiotics, and no routine intubation since **positive pressure ventilation** (bagged breaths) drives air through the fistula. Distal tube advancement, fistula balloon, or **gastrostomy** (stomach vent to water seal) serve as rescue.

nodes.label: Upright prone nursing with sump suction
Rescue with gastrostomy to water seal

steps.say: The chest is opened on the side opposite the aortic arch, working outside the pleura throughout. Right thoracotomy suits a left arch while either side suits a right arch. Dividing the azygos vein, closing the 1 to 2 millimetre fistula stump at once, and mobilising the upper pouch widely are completing the repair.
steps.tx: Side follows the arch, with right **thoracotomy** (chest opening) suiting a left aortic arch while either side suits a right arch. Repair is extrapleural with **azygos vein** (arch vein) division and immediate absorbable closure of the **1** to **2** mm fistula stump, then primary **anastomosis** (joined gullet) with a widely mobilised upper pouch and gentle handling of the lower pouch.

steps.say: The Spitz score remains a predictor of survival from just two bedside facts, and parents grasp it quickly. Babies over 1500 grams without major cardiac disease are reaching 97 percent survival. Either risk factor alone drops survival to 59 percent, while both together leave 22 percent.
steps.tx: The **Spitz classification** (survival score) predicts outcome by **birth weight** (over **1500** g) and **cardiac anomaly** (major heart disease): over 1500 g with no major lesion at **97** percent, either factor alone at **59** percent, and both at **22** percent, guiding counselling before repair.

steps.say: Warn families that the story continues after a perfect repair, because the joined gullet stays sensitive for years. Reflux remains common in 25 to 50 percent, stricture in 15 to 30 percent, leak in 10 to 20 percent and tracheomalacia in 8 to 15 percent. Thoracoscopy with preoperative bronchoscopy is now standard.
steps.tx: Sequelae are reflux in **25** to **50** percent, **anastomotic stricture** (join narrowing) in **15** to **30** percent, **anastomotic leak** (join leakage) in **10** to **20** percent and **tracheomalacia** (floppy windpipe) in **8** to **15** percent. Thoracoscopy with preoperative bronchoscopy for tracheomalacia and second fistula is now standard.
